text: Hongkong, Monday, Sept. 20, 1926.

label: text
text: At first sight it may be regarded "as distinctly encouraging to learn from Mr. Eugene Chen, in the course of a letter addressed by him to the British Consul-General,—the text of which appears elsewhere in this issue—that arrangements have been made to end the boycott on or before October 10 (probably by the end of September), and that these arrangements "have been made with the Strike Committee." Had Mr. Chen's communication contained no more and no less than this, we would to-day have been in a position to congratulate him on the best stroke of work he has done since he assumed his present office in Canton.

label: text
text: Unfortunately extraneous matters are introduced by Mr. Eugene Chen, which gives the whole "arrangements to end the boycott" a totally different aspect. His letter, in the first place, is headed, "Republic of China. Nationalist Government. Ministry of Foreign Affairs." To the Powers there is only one Government in China, and its headquarters are still in Peking and not in Canton. Moreover, as the boycott originated in Canton why should Mr. Eugene Chen seek now to identify with its settlement the "Nationalist Government of the Republic of China?" The boycott is no affair of the Peking Government, and to attempt to insinuate otherwise is scarcely politic, to say the least of it. As it stands, his letter cannot possibly be replied.

label: text
text: to, apart altogether from the other extraneous matter which he has succeeded in introducing.

label: text
text: Mr. Eugene Chen proceeds to connect the "arrangements to end the boycott" with the intimidation of the intention to impose certain tariffs, for the authority for which he seeks to bind the "proper Chinese authorities"—presumably with their headquarters also in Canton. These special taxes follow in the main those laid down in the Washington Convention, to which nine Powers are signatory, and under the provisions of which the Tariff Conference has already held several sessions in Peking and other centres. A new tax, however, not mentioned in the Washington Convention, is the "special production or producers' tax on exports."

label: text
text: It is so obvious that proposals of this kind cannot be made with the Government having its centre in Canton, which for the purposes of the Treaty is studiously incorporated with “China,” the recognised capital of which is Peking, that they can be dismissed from further thought right away. Mr. Eugene Chen must be aware that no single Power can possibly acquiesce in the imposition of such tariffs without the unanimous concurrence of the other eight signatories to the Washington Convention. Great Britain alone cannot do so, even if the war situation was so to develop as eventually to warrant Mr. Eugene Chen speaking on behalf of the “Nationalist Government of the Republic of China.” Therefore, the only possible course of procedure for the Consul-General in Canton is to refer the letter to Peking for its consideration. And of course, Peking could only reply that the boycott engineered and carried out in Canton is no concern of it and that, moreover, Canton cannot be recognised as the official seat of the Nationalist Government of the Republic of China.

label: text
text: It appears that Mr. Eugene Chen, if he is still anxious to end the boycott on or about the date he mentions, will either have to consult the Strike Committee again or let the arrangements stand without any reference to Customs tariffs or the Nationalist Government of the Republic of China.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOONCAKE FEAST.

label: paragraph_title
text: TO-MORROW'S BIG CHINESE FESTIVAL.

label: text
text: AN EMPEROR'S CONCUBINE.

label: text
text: Mooncake Feast, or Mid-Autumn Festival, or Chung-chin chief, to give its classical rendering, falls this year on Tuesday (to-morrow), the 15th day of the 8th moon.

label: text
text: Tradition places its origin about 2,150 B.C. when lived, the famous archer-Emperor "Hao I" (Hao Ngai in Cantonese).

label: text
text: He shot nine of the ten suns illuminating the heavens when the sun-god besought him not to make a bull's eye of the tenth. For this boon he was given a potion which would make him immortal with a home in the sun.

label: text
text: Before he could take the potion which had to be prepared in an urn at night with devout prayers meanwhile, a naughty concubine by name of Sheung. Ngo drained the last drop while her spouse slept through the watch-night service.

label: text
text: Light as a fairy, the woman fled to the moon to escape the archer's wrath.

label: text
text: Every year she returns to mother earth and moon-cakes are eaten in her honour.

label: text
text: Thrown Out of Moon!

label: text
text: This episode has been commercialised into a favourite stage-play being one of the star-numbers of Mei Lan-fang's repertoire. Mei will be remembered as the famous Northern actor who was down here in 1922.

label: text
text: The legend has been slightly lengthened and ends up with Hao I being thrown out of the moon after a hot pursuit of his concubine.

label: text
text: It is a harvest festival in that the tea-houses reap their annual harvest. Moon-shaped cakes with wonderful ingredients are made months ahead of the festival and shipped to all parts of the world where Chinese are to be found.

label: text
text: Chinese delight in these delicacies. Another aspect is the making and sale of beautiful lanterns with which Chinatown will be decorated to-night. Actually the men-folk take little note of the religious side of the festival except to organise a feast at West Point.

label: paragraph_title
text: CORRESPONDENCE

label: paragraph_title
text: WHY USE "MADAME" FOR "MRS."?

label: text
text: LOCAL APPELLATIONS

label: text
text:
[To the Editor of the "China Mail"]
Sir,—Can anyone explain why Hong Kong journalists apparently make a point of designating Mrs. Sun Yat-sen, Mrs. Chang-Kai-shek and the wives of certain other notorious Chinese militants. "Madame"? It certainly is a curious custom and it is difficult to find an explanation for same.

label: text
text: Equally curious is the practice adopted by the authorities of Hong Kong and the majority of the Treaty Ports who appear to make a point of naming thorough-fares after the cities of Peking, Canton and other cess-pools of iniquity.

label: text
text: One would imagine that the average pedestrian would welcome a change of names. To be constantly reminded that such places exist is not exactly exhiliating.

label: text

label: text
text: Questioned by Mr. H. S. Fitzroy (for the defence) as to whether if a man thought he had leprosy and allowed his mind to dwell on it overmuch he might develop insanity, witness replied that it was possible but improbable unless the man in question had a bad mental balance.

label: paragraph_title
text: WAR TERRORS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
MINES TO BLOW OUT
WUCHANG?

label: paragraph_title
text: BESIEGED FOREIGNERS.

label: text
text: It is reported that plans are afoot to mine the Wuchang wall. A tunnel is already underway. To-day the food situation in Wuchang is most critical. Twenty-six foreigners are confined in the city whereof. 21 are Americans, three British and two Germans. These foreigners have previously been allowed to send out letters to Hankow friends but after to-day all mail communication will be stopped by order of the local authorities. The Wuhan Chambers of Commerce have intimated to the Southerners that it is impossible for them to raise further loans as their coffers are already drained. Anxiety is now felt in the Chamber circles as to how the refusal will be met.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hankow Conditions:

label: text
text: It was reported from Hankow on Friday evening that Wuchang was holding out.

label: text
text: Fighting occurred near Kuang-shui, to which place trains are no longer running.

label: text
text: It is reported that the Wu Sheng Kuan Pass is strongly fortified.

label: text
text: No vessels are permitted to enter Hankow port without inspection, and then only between six o'clock in the morning and six o'clock in the evening.

label: text
text: The Labour Unions are less active, and some factories are reopening.

label: text
text: It is reported that Yen Hsi-shan has remitted to Marshal Wu Pei-fu $300,000, and is sending to Hsinyang 10,000 grenades.—Reuter.
